blocks.text: vLLM is a high-throughput serving framework for large language models, built specifically to maximize GPU utilization and request throughput for production inference, one of the four major serving frameworks covered in this module alongside Ollama, TensorRT-LLM, and TGI.

This topic covers vLLM core innovation, PagedAttention, how continuous batching improves throughput over naive batching, and its OpenAI-compatible API that makes it a straightforward drop-in for many existing applications.
1. What vLLM Provides
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785472763105-385838550.png

vLLM takes an exported model, covered in the previous topic, and serves it through an optimized inference engine designed specifically to handle many concurrent requests efficiently, a meaningful step beyond simply running a model directly with the training-time libraries covered earlier in this module.
2. PagedAttention, vLLM Core Innovation
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785472763106-34617611.png

Generation requires storing a growing key-value cache per request, naive implementations allocate this memory in large contiguous blocks, wasting significant memory to unused reserved space, PagedAttention instead manages this cache in smaller, flexible pages, similar in spirit to virtual memory paging in operating systems, dramatically improving memory efficiency and allowing many more concurrent requests.

blocks.title: This is the single biggest reason vLLM gained widespread adoption
blocks.content: PagedAttention memory efficiency directly translates into serving significantly more concurrent requests on the same hardware compared to naive KV cache management, a major practical throughput win.

blocks.text: 3. Continuous Batching for GPU Utilization
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785472763106-200371069.png

vLLM continuously admits new requests into an in-progress batch as soon as GPU capacity allows, rather than waiting for a full batch to accumulate or for the current batch to fully finish, keeping the GPU consistently busy and significantly improving overall throughput.
4. Fixed Batching vs Continuous Batching
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785472763106-845234262.png

Traditional fixed batching groups a set number of requests together and processes them as one unit, requests that finish early sit idle waiting for the rest, continuous batching lets each request join and leave the processing batch independently, avoiding this wasted idle time entirely.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Batching Style","Behavior"],"rows":[["Fixed batching","Waits for a full batch, requests idle until the batch completes"],["Continuous batching","Requests join and leave independently, minimal idle time"]]}

blocks.text: 5. An OpenAI-Compatible API
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785472763107-759820242.png

vLLM exposes an API compatible with the widely used OpenAI chat completion interface, letting applications already built against that interface switch to a self-hosted vLLM deployment with minimal code changes, a practical convenience that lowered the adoption barrier significantly.
6. vLLM Compared to Other Serving Frameworks

blocks.alt: vLLM Compared to Other Serving Frameworks
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785472763107-69340949.png

vLLM, TGI, and TensorRT-LLM, both covered in later topics, all target high-throughput serving but make different tradeoffs, vLLM emphasizes broad model support and ease of deployment alongside its PagedAttention efficiency, while TensorRT-LLM trades broader compatibility for maximum performance on specific NVIDIA hardware through deeper hardware-specific compilation.
7. Serving LoRA Adapters Directly Through vLLM

blocks.alt: Serving LoRA Adapters Directly Through vLLM
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785472763107-340777578.png

vLLM supports serving multiple LoRA adapters directly, connecting to the adapter loading concepts covered in an earlier topic, letting a single vLLM deployment serve several task-specific fine-tuned behaviors from one shared base model without needing to merge each adapter into a separate full model.
8. When vLLM Is the Right Choice

vLLM tends to fit production deployments that need to serve many concurrent requests efficiently on GPU hardware, with broad model architecture support and a familiar API surface, a strong general-purpose default among the serving frameworks covered in this module for most GPU-based production serving needs.
9. Practical Deployment Considerations

Running vLLM effectively still requires choosing appropriate hardware, GPU memory needs to fit both model weights and the PagedAttention-managed KV cache, and tuning serving-level parameters like maximum batch size and tensor parallelism, covered in the earlier Distributed Training Techniques module, to match the actual traffic pattern being served.
Worked Example

A team deploying their fine-tuned assistant for production traffic switches from a naive custom inference script to vLLM, immediately gaining continuous batching and PagedAttention memory efficiency without changing their application code, since they adopt vLLM OpenAI-compatible API as a drop-in replacement for their existing API calls.

They further deploy several task-specific LoRA adapters, covered in earlier modules, directly through vLLM adapter serving support, letting one vLLM instance handle multiple customer-specific behaviors rather than requiring a separate deployment per adapter.
Common Mistakes

items: Running a model with a naive custom inference loop when vLLM continuous batching would substantially improve throughput
Not accounting for PagedAttention KV cache memory needs when sizing GPU hardware for a deployment
Merging every adapter into a separate full model instead of using vLLM native multi-adapter serving support
Choosing vLLM for a use case that actually needs the maximum hardware-specific performance TensorRT-LLM, covered in a later topic, provides

blocks.text: Practice

For a production serving scenario you are familiar with or could imagine, list the specific advantages, PagedAttention memory efficiency, continuous batching, OpenAI-compatible API, multi-adapter serving, that would make vLLM a good fit compared to a naive custom serving script.
Key Takeaway

vLLM serves large language models efficiently at scale through PagedAttention memory management and continuous batching, exposing a familiar OpenAI-compatible API and native support for serving multiple LoRA adapters from one base model, making it a strong general-purpose default among the serving frameworks covered in this module for GPU-based production deployments.
